reasoning_traces.think:
The TrajSV framework operates by first extracting trajectory information from broadcast sports videos using a motion tracking pipeline such as FairMOT, then rasterizing these trajectories into binary field grids. These grids are processed by CRNet which combines them with visual features from X-CLIP to form clip-level representations. The VRNet aggregates these clip representations into video-level embeddings using a transformer architecture with multi-head attention. The entire system is trained using a triple contrastive loss that encourages alignment of representations across different levels (within clips, between clips, and between videos). This design enables unsupervised learning of rich semantic representations that can be used for retrieval, action spotting, and captioning. However, the reliance on synthetic noise-corrupted queries for validation introduces a closed-world bias, limiting its applicability to real-world open-world similarity search scenarios.
